# Toast

> A polite heads-up that something just happened. It lives on the page up front, so screen readers actually hear it.

`<slab-toast>` · Overlays · built on `[role=status]`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/toast/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/toast.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-toast duration="5000">Changes saved</slab-toast>

<script type="module">
  document.querySelector('slab-toast').show();
</script>
```

## Keyboard

| Key    | What it does                                                                                    |
| ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| F6     | Moves focus to the open toast shown most recently, and from inside it, back to where focus was. |
| Escape | Dismisses the toast while focus is in it, and moves focus back to where it was.                 |

## Elements

### `<slab-toast>`

Import `slab-elements/toast.js` to register it.

A toast with no visual styles: a polite `[role=status]` live region that lives on the page for good and is shown and dismissed rather than added and removed.

Put it on the page up front, not when there's something to say. A live region only announces what's inserted into it after screenreaders have found it, so a region added along with its content is usually read by nobody. The region inside this one is rendered, empty, as soon as the host is connected. Its content goes in the default slot, and the slot is only rendered by `show()`, which is the insertion screenreaders announce. `show()` again, with new content or the same, announces it again.

The region is a `popover="manual"` in the top layer, shown when the host is connected and raised again by each `show()`, so it sits above a dialog opened since. The top layer doesn't get it out of a modal dialog's inertness, though: everything outside the dialog is inert, and inert content isn't announced or clickable. So a toast for something that happens in a modal dialog belongs inside the dialog. While dismissed, the region stays in the accessibility tree but is hidden visually.

`duration` dismisses the toast that many milliseconds after it's shown. 0 keeps it until it's dismissed. The countdown pauses while the pointer is over the toast or focus is in it, and starts over when both have left, so no one loses a toast they're reading or about to act on.

A toast with something to act on, such as an Undo button or a link, is never dismissed on a timer, whatever `duration` says. Someone who needs longer to get to it, or is getting there by keyboard from across the page, would otherwise lose the action along with the toast (WCAG 2.2.1). Give it a way to be dismissed, or dismiss it once it's been acted on.

A toast is in the top layer, nowhere near where focus usually is, so F6 moves focus to the open toast shown most recently, and F6 from inside it moves focus back to where it was. That's how react-aria's toasts are reached. Dismissing a toast with focus in it also moves focus back.

Escape dismisses it while focus is in it.

However it's dismissed, by Escape, its timer or `dismiss()`, it dispatches "dismiss" first. Cancel that to keep it shown, as Alert's can be.

Style it through its part and through `:state(open)`. Where it sits on the page, and whether several stack, is left to the styles around it.

#### Attributes

| Name       | Type     | Default | Description                                                              |
| ---------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `duration` | `number` | `5000`  | Milliseconds until it dismisses itself. 0 keeps it until it's dismissed. |

#### Properties

| Name               | Type      | Description         |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------------------- |
| `open` (read-only) | `boolean` | Whether it's shown. |

#### Methods

| Signature               | Description |
| ----------------------- | ----------- |
| `dismiss(): void`       | Hides it.   |
| `show(): Promise<void>` | Shows it.   |

#### Events

| Name      | Type          | Description                                                                                                          |
| --------- | ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dismiss` | `Event`       | When it's dismissed, by Escape, its timer or `dismiss()`. Cancel it to keep it shown.                                |
| `toggle`  | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does. |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description      |
| --------- | ------------------- | ---------------- |
| (default) | `Element \| string` | What's announced |

#### CSS parts

| Name     | Description              |
| -------- | ------------------------ |
| `region` | The region it's shown in |

#### CSS states

| Name           | Description       |
| -------------- | ----------------- |
| `:state(open)` | While it's shown. |
